solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Warning to dispose of uranium particle that's charged

indicators.note: to dispose of something is to get rid of it, so the named element is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: a warning is a caution
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A hazard notice telling workers how to get rid of radioactive uranium safely.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the U out of CAUTION to leave CATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A cation is an ion carrying a positive electrical charge, so it is a charged particle.

clue.text: Stop using computers? Don't be ridiculous!

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: give up IT, information technology
second meaning: an exclamation of disbelief

explanation.walkthrough: IT stands for information technology, so quitting computers is coming off IT; the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Come off it is an idiom used to tell someone they are talking nonsense, which matches the exclamation.

clue.text: Still ignoring limits of French and Spanish accent

indicators.note: ignoring the limits means skipping the end letters, so only the inner part of that word survives

blocks.note: the inside of still, without its first and last letters
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Something about French and Spanish speech, as if comparing their regional pronunciations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish accent' looks like a way of speaking, but it is a written mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy mark over the n in Spanish words such as señor, a diacritic or accent.

clue.text: Brave to not open shop outside hotel in part of city

indicators.note: a word that does not open has lost its opening, so its first letter goes
the shop being outside something means it wraps around it

blocks.note: bold, meaning brave, without its first letter
a deli is a delicatessen shop
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A bold decision not to open a shop beside a hotel in some urban district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is first turned into a synonym, and it is that synonym which loses its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Delhi is the historic walled district of the Indian capital, so it is part of a city.

clue.text: Not mandatory to answer, OK?

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: a question you may pass on rather than answer
second meaning: adequate, acceptable, good enough

explanation.surface: An exam paper note saying a question is optional, followed by a query asking if that is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is whimsical: a question you are allowed to pass is literally pass-able.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means satisfactory but not outstanding, which matches the casual sense of OK.

clue.text: Scouts, as a rule, messed up part of basic training

indicators.note: something messed up is in disarray, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Scouts usually making a mess of their early drills.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault course is an obstacle circuit that army recruits run as part of their initial training.

clue.text: Search with detective, Norwegian, say

blocks.note: to scan is to search
DI is Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police hunt involving a detective and a Norwegian suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandi is informal for Scandinavian, and a Norwegian is one example of a Scandinavian person.

clue.text: Strip vehicle of sports equipment and phone

blocks.note: a bat is used in cricket or baseball
a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.surface: Stripping a vehicle of its sporting gear and phone, as a thief might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like a verb meaning remove, but it is a comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Batmobile is Batman's car in the comic strips, so it is a vehicle from a strip.

clue.text: Spooky European lake

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A haunted-looking lake somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening in an uncanny way, which is what spooky means.

clue.text: Look into doctor, say — that's nice to hear

indicators.note: one thing going into another puts it inside, so the first word sits within the second

blocks.note: a doctor is an example of a medic
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A patient asked to examine a doctor and finding the experience pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look into' reads as investigate, but it is the word look going into the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic music has a pleasing tune, something agreeable to listen to.

clue.text: Rue cooking cheesy samples?

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Regretting the cheese tasters you prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rue' looks like the verb regret, but it is French for street.
explanation.definitionFit: The Champs-Élysées is the famous avenue in Paris, and rue is the French word for street.

clue.text: Appetiser and dessert — rest is sent back outside unfinished

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its ending, so the last letter of that word is dropped
sending something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run from right to left
being outside something means surrounding it, so these letters wrap around the dessert

blocks.note: the word rest with its final letter cut off
a tart is a sweet pastry served as dessert

explanation.surface: A diner ordering the first and last courses and sending the remainder back to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened, reversed word is split in two so that it wraps around the dessert on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter is the first course of a meal, which is another name for an appetiser.

clue.text: Very large award set to be reduced

indicators.note: reducing something makes it shorter, so the last letter of that word is trimmed away

blocks.note: the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire
the word set missing its final letter

explanation.surface: An honour whose value or presentation is about to be scaled down.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes someone extremely overweight, so very large in body size.

clue.text: Muscle into a capital place for water sports

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside, so the muscle sits within the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
quad is short for quadriceps, the thigh muscle
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Muscling your way into a capital city to find a venue for swimming and boating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscle into' reads as a verb phrase meaning force your way in, but the muscle is a noun naming the thigh.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquadrome is a lake or complex built for boating, swimming and other water-based activities.

clue.text: Route requiring soft touch to enter ferry harbour at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the two words just before it
entering means going inside, so the soft touch is placed within the other letters

blocks.note: first letter of ferry
a light touch is a soft one
a pat is a gentle touch
first letter of harbour

explanation.surface: Docking a ferry calls for a gentle hand at the start of its journey into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft touch' looks like one phrase meaning a pushover, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight path is the course an aircraft follows, so it is a route through the air.

clue.text: Ancient creature's fertilizer held by one academic

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so the fertilizer sits within the academic letters

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
guano is seabird or bat droppings used as manure
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A professor keeping a dinosaur's droppings for study.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur, an ancient creature of the Cretaceous period.

clue.text: Member steps under the bar briefly?

indicators.note: saying something briefly cuts it short, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: the limbo is a dance where you lean back and shuffle beneath a low bar

explanation.surface: Someone stepping beneath a bar, as if a club member ducking under it.
explanation.walkthrough: LIMBO loses its final O.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb, an arm or a leg, is a member of the body in the older anatomical sense.

clue.text: Two bachelors embracing the short lady — that's David's wife!

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so the bachelors surround the middle letters
short means cut down, so the last letter of the preceding word is lost

blocks.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, twice
the without its last letter
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Two single men hugging a petite woman who turns out to be married to David.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' applies only to 'the'; 'lady' stays whole. BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Bathsheba married King David after he had her husband Uriah killed.

clue.text: US college groups picked up kind of marine creature

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: frats are American fraternities
-ish means somewhat or kind of

explanation.surface: American student societies collecting some sort of sea animal.
explanation.walkthrough: FRATS reversed gives STARF, then ISH is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A starfish is a star-shaped echinoderm living on the sea bed, a marine creature.

clue.text: Excursion in direction of ancient city

blocks.note: to means heading towards
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A trip heading off to some ruined city of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a trip or outing taken for pleasure, like an excursion.

clue.text: Carriage left chaps in debt, with billions lost

indicators.note: something lost has gone missing, so the billions are taken away from that word
being in something means sitting inside it, so the left chaps are put within the debt

blocks.note: debt without its B
port is the left side of a ship
chaps are men
B is the abbreviation for billions, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Men abandoned in debt after a fortune has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a vehicle but means bearing. PORTMEN goes inside DEBT once its B (billions) is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage can mean the way a person holds their body, which is their deportment or posture.

clue.text: A large tree from the mountains

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes
a pine is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A big conifer growing up in the high country.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine describes things belonging to high mountains, originally the Alps, so of mountain origin.

clue.text: Maybe try to get gold coat for ship?

blocks.note: to mine is to dig in an attempt to extract gold or other ore
a coat of paint is a layer

explanation.surface: A prospector hoping to strike gold and buy a fancy coat with the proceeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A minelayer is a naval vessel designed to lay explosive mines at sea, so it is a kind of ship.

clue.text: Tricks graduate with dodgy CGI

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so these letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film graduate passing off shoddy computer effects as illusions.
explanation.walkthrough: CGI is computer-generated imagery, the special effects in films.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is the art of conjuring, made up of tricks and illusions performed for an audience.

clue.text: Inspector concerned with craft heading the wrong way

indicators.note: travelling the wrong way means going backwards, so this word is read from end to start

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a sub, a submarine, is a craft

explanation.surface: A detective investigating a vessel that was sailing in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector John Rebus is the Edinburgh detective in Ian Rankin's crime novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebus is the surname of a famous fictional police inspector, so the name stands for that inspector.

clue.text: Shows a yellow card to rugby players hiding ball

indicators.note: hiding something keeps it inside out of sight, so the ball goes within the players

blocks.note: the Boks, or Springboks, are South Africa's national rugby team
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A referee cautioning rugby players who are concealing the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside BOKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee who books a player records an offence, usually by showing a yellow card.

clue.text: Superhuman kid playing with Lego

indicators.note: a child playing with bricks rearranges them, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child absorbed in building toys, imagining being a superhero.
explanation.definitionFit: Godlike means having the qualities of a god, which is beyond human, so superhuman.

clue.text: Essence of chapter missing from long book

indicators.note: something missing from a whole has been taken out of it, so the chapter's letter is absent

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter, the letter taken out
an epic is a work of great length
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: The core of a lengthy volume minus one chapter that has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: EPIC TOME loses its C, giving EPITOME.
explanation.definitionFit: The epitome of something is its perfect embodiment, the quintessence or essence of it.

clue.text: Notices a flailing paddler

indicators.note: flailing means thrashing about wildly, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spots a swimmer or wader thrashing around in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoeist propels a canoe with a paddle, so is literally a paddler.

clue.text: Smokes his hash partially with this?

definitions.text: Smokes his hash partially with this?

indicators.note: partially means only part of the words is used, so the target sits inside a run of the clue

blocks.note: found spanning the end of smokes, all of his and the start of hash

explanation.surface: A man partly smoking his cannabis through some device.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a shisha is what he could be smoking it with.
explanation.definitionFit: A shisha is a water pipe used for smoking flavoured tobacco, and sometimes hash, so it fits as the device.
